title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: these are Grothendieck's unpublished 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', which develop a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type theory. The data are as follows.

- A profinite group 𝔊 contains two distinguished torsion elements ρ and σ. These are presumably of orders 2 and 3, the elliptic generators of a PSL(2)-type quotient written 𝔊_{0,3}^+. There is also a procyclic subgroup L_1 = ⟨t_1⟩ generated by a 'twist' t_1.
- A group 𝓜 acts on it, with a subgroup 𝓜[0] and a surjection 𝒢[0] → 𝓜[0] with kernel J.

The previous page attaches to each u_0 ∈ 𝒢[0] a pair of cocycle values α(u_0), β(u_0). These satisfy αρ(α)^{-1} = [u,ρ] and βσ(β)^{-1} = [u,σ]. The page then shows that they descend to 𝓜[0] exactly when α^Π(δ_0) and β^Π(δ_0) lie in Ker φ for δ_0 ∈ J; this is hypothesis (20).

This page draws the consequences.

(21) The hypothesis gives maps α, β : 𝓜[0] ⇉ 𝔊. They factor the earlier formulas (19).

(22) For each u ∈ 𝓜[0], u(ρ) = int(α)ρ and u(σ) = int(β)σ. So u sends each elliptic generator to a conjugate of itself; this replaces the earlier normalisation (2').

(23)–(25) Put ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} and η = βσβ^{-1}σ^{-1}. Then (22) becomes u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ. Equivalently ξ = [u,ρ] and η = [u,σ], with commutators taken in the semidirect product 𝔊 ⋊ 𝓜[0].

(26) Moreover ξ = η·t_1^ν with ν = (μ−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ, where μ is the multiplier ('multiplicateur') of u. This is inherited from the analogous relation in 𝔊_{0,3}^+. The exponent (μ−1)/2 is exactly the 'm = (λ−1)/2' of the GT hexagon relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1. So (26) is an 'elliptic' (order-2/order-3) incarnation of the hexagon.

(27) For this to make sense, the multiplier character χ^𝒢 : 𝒢 → Ẑ* is assumed to factor through 𝓜. Thus every u ∈ 𝓜 has a cyclotomic-type multiplier.

(28) Finally Grothendieck considers 𝓜[0] → Aut(𝔊), u ↦ int(u)|𝔊. He begins to observe, completed on the next page, two things:
- ξ and η depend only on the image of u in Aut(𝔊), the group 𝓜'[0], whereas α and β need not when the action is not faithful.
- Hence one gets a map from a subgroup of Norm_{Aut(𝔊)}(L_0) to the solution set Σ_{𝔊,ρ,σ} of the 'loop equation': pairs (ξ,η) with ξρ ~ ρ, ησ ~ σ and η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1.

Purpose: to parametrise automorphisms of a Teichmüller-type profinite group, the GT-like 'Teichmüller tower' automorphisms, by solutions of an equation in two unknowns. This is the abstract counterpart of describing GT as pairs (λ,f) satisfying the 2-, 3- and 5-cycle relations.
errors: No outright error. The consistency checks work: (23) with ρ(α) = ραρ^{-1} gives ξρ = αρα^{-1}, which matches (22) and (24); (25) matches (16) of the previous page.

Relation (26) is asserted, not derived ('provient de la relation analogue dans 𝔊_{0,3}^+'). Its validity depends on the convention t_1 = ρσ (or similar) and on choosing α, β normalised compatibly. Otherwise ν is only determined modulo the ambiguity coming from the centralisers T_ρ and T_σ noted on the previous page.
The reference '(2')' and the factorisation of (19) rely on earlier pages not shown.

ideas.what: Descending cocycle data α, β from 𝒢[0] to the quotient 𝓜[0] and expressing the action on the elliptic generators by u(ρ) = int(α)ρ, u(σ) = int(β)σ
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT / Galois on profinite PSL2(Z) or B_3 via conjugation of the torsion (elliptic) generators
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse beyond a sketch; Longue Marche treats related material only partially (unsure of exact overlap)

ideas.what: Relation ξ = η t_1^{(μ−1)/2} between the two conjugating elements, with μ the cyclotomic multiplier
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon (3-cycle) relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, with m = (λ−1)/2
ideas.where_published: Possibly anticipated in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure

ideas.what: Passing to the image 𝓜'[0] in Aut(𝔊): ξ, η are defined on 𝓜'[0] while α, β need not be, giving a map from a subgroup of the normaliser of L_0 to the solution set Σ_{𝔊,ρ,σ} of the loop equation
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of (outer) automorphisms of a Teichmüller-type profinite group by solutions of a GT-type equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld / Ihara / Lochak–Schneps for GT-hat; the general abstract version is not standardly credited

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the 'loop equation' abstractly for any profinite group 𝔊 with elliptic elements ρ, σ, a procyclic L_1 and a multiplier character. He sets up a map from automorphisms normalising L_0 to its solution set, which suggests a general GT-type theory attached to arbitrary such data (𝔊, ρ, σ, t_1), not just F̂_2 / B̂_3. Whether this map is bijective or injective in general is left open here.
missed.quote: ξ = η t_1^ν où ν = (μ−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ (μ le multiplicateur de u) qui provient de la relation analogue dans 𝔊_{0,3}^+
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Versions of GT attached to quotients or finite-index variants of B̂_3 / PSL2(Ẑ) (e.g. 'GT-shadows', Dessins-type quotients, Pop/Minamide work on anabelian GT) are active topics. This page is an early abstract framework for them, though the core relation itself is well known.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the order-2/order-3 form of the GT hexagon relation with the exponent (μ−1)/2, now standard via Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak–Schneps. What is mildly notable is Grothendieck's abstract, axiomatic setting (an arbitrary 𝓜 acting on 𝔊 with a multiplier, descent from 𝒢[0] via the kernel J, and passage to the image in Aut). This is an unpublished framework, but not a surprising result.
transcription_corrections: 'factorisant (19), et satisfaisant dans' is probably 'factorisant (19), et satisfaisant donc'.
In (22) the struck-out letter before ∈ 𝓜[0] is a deleted 'u'/'tt'; the condition reads 'pour u ∈ 𝓜[0], α = α̲(u), β = β̲(u)'.
The struck label next to 𝒢 → Ẑ* is a crossed-out '(19)'/'(??)'; the multiplier map has no surviving number.
Above the last line the insertion is 'ou mieux (24)'. The line continues roughly 'on voit sur (22) ou mieux (24) que ... comme quand on connaît [ρ,σ] ...', continued on the next page.
In (26) the symbol is t_1 (not ℓ_1); the parenthesis reads '(μ le multiplicateur de u)'.
